items.title: Call to Order
notes: Mayor Watters welcomed everyone and called the meeting to order.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Jefferson read the land acknowledgement.

items.title: Addendums and Corrections to the Agenda
notes: None.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest Under the Municipal Conflict of Interest
notes: Act
None declared.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the County Budget was passed with a 3.7% increase. He indicated the increase will mean an additional $27 per year for every $100,000 worth of assessed residential property value. Mayor Watters also noted the County of Wellington is pursuing funding opportunities in order to support the climate change adaption plan.
Mayor Watters also responded to a question regarding the involvement of the area municipalities in climate change initiatives.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Members of Council provided updates and highlights of the recent activities of the advisory committees, including the Fergus BIA and Farm Safety.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. However, any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate discussion.
Councillor Wilton requested a staff overview of item 7.6.

Ian Duncan Water Conservation Coordinator provided an update on the 2024 water conservation program, ongoing conservation efforts and 2025 program goals and future conservation program initiatives. He outlined the branding initiative, the education and outreach program, the various conservation programs including the water audit program, toilet rebate program, water efficiency building guidelines, etc., and the updated outdoor water use by-law.
Ian Duncan responded to questions regarding the current uptake of the toilet rebate program and potential expansion of the program.
Mayor Watters asked if there where any further questions.
Councillor Adams posed a question to the Municipal By-law Enforcement Officer regarding the number of complains with respect to long grass and weeds.
Councillor Jefferson asked for a brief overview of the Annual Drinking Water Report which was provided by Dino Masiero, Manager of Water Services and Environmental Sustainability.

items.title: Bridge and Transportation Network: Preliminary Preferred Alternative for
notes: Bridges 2-WG, 3-E, 5-E and 7-E

Report from A. Dickieson, Engineering Services Coordinator Adam Dickieson, Engineering Technologist outlined the project scope and study area. He reviewed the impacts of the closures to transportation and the various options to repair, to remove or to replace.
He reviewed the public and area resident consultation process undertaken.

Adam Dickieson responded to questions regarding the differences in the community’s response, the timing of the replacement, impact to the farming practices, additional signage installed and the lack of impact to the emergency response time.

items.title: Fees and Charges By-law Amendment
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report.
